cards.name: The Olive-Wood Test
cards.rules: Target permanent you control gains indestructible until end of turn. If it's legendary, scry 1.
cards.story: Book XXIII / Penelope's test turns on the secret that their marriage bed was built around a living olive trunk and cannot simply be moved.
cards.credit: Art: “Ulysses and Penelope” · Francesco Primaticcio · Wildenstein Collection, New York · Wikimedia Commons
cards.storyTarget: Book XXIII / the immovable marriage bed proves Odysseus's identity to Penelope.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Only the couple knows how the rooted bed was made, so knowledge of its immovability becomes the decisive recognition test.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: A clean common relationship card for Penelope and the legendary Olive-Wood Bed: it literally makes a permanent impossible to move or destroy for the turn.

cards.name: Telemachus, Young Heir
cards.rules: Heroic — Whenever you cast a spell that targets Telemachus, put a +1/+1 counter on Telemachus.
cards.story: Books I–IV / maturation
cards.credit: Art: “Helen Recognising Telemachus, Son of Odysseus” · Jean-Jacques Lagrenée · Hermitage Museum · Wikimedia Commons
cards.storyTarget: Books I–IV / maturation
cards.flavorStoryElement: Books I–IV / maturation
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Strong match: the card clearly represents Books I–IV / maturation, and Heroic supports that story even if the execution is somewhat general.

cards.name: Traveler's Amulet
cards.rules: {1}, Sacrifice this artifact: Search your library for a basic land card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle.
cards.story: At the inland end of Tiresias’s prophecy, Odysseus plants the oar and establishes a shrine to Poseidon, completing the ritual that carries a seafarer’s burden into a land that does not know the sea.
cards.credit: Art: Nikias Painter, late 5th c. BCE · The Met
cards.changeStatus: story-retheme-v2 · art-review · flavor-redesign-v1 · task5-post-odyssey-collapse-v1 · inland-shrine-rebuild-v1 · art-acceptance-v1
cards.storyTarget: At the inland end of Tiresias’s prophecy, Odysseus plants the oar and establishes a shrine to Poseidon, completing the ritual that carries a seafarer’s burden into a land that does not know the sea.
cards.flavorStoryElement: The inland-oar journey ends in a shrine and sacrifice to Poseidon among people who do not know the sea.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Excellent mechanical match: the carried object is sacrificed to find a new land, so Traveler's Amulet's real rules become a literal pilgrimage-and-shrine fixing card while the inland-oar package collapses to one identity.

cards.name: Sustain the Household
cards.rules: Constellation — Whenever an enchantment you control enters, put a quest counter on this enchantment and create a 1/1 white Human Citizen creature token. This ability triggers only once each turn. Then if this enchantment has three or more quest counters on it, sacrifice it. When you do, you gain 3 life.
cards.story: Books II–XIX / the Ithacan household survives long absence through repeated work, delayed decisions, and people continuing their duties.
cards.credit: Art: Achilles Painter, ca. 440 BCE · The Met
cards.storyTarget: Books II–XIX / household continuity through long absence and repeated work.
cards.storySourceBand: Odyssey Books II and XIX; household composite
cards.flavorStoryElement: The house endures because work continues day after day while absence stretches on.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Constellation turns repeated household work into people and time counters; the third counter completes an endurance challenge without inventing a literal armed watch.

cards.name: Athena's Intervention
cards.rules: Exile target creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control. Scry 1.
cards.story: Athena's protection / revelation
cards.credit: Art: Anonymous, 17th century · Rijksmuseum
cards.storyTarget: Athena's protection / revelation
cards.flavorStoryElement: Book XIII / Athena reveals Ithaca to Odysseus, then alters his appearance so he can enter his own kingdom unrecognized
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Strong match: the card clearly represents Book XIII / Athena reveals Ithaca to Odysseus, then alters his appearance so he can enter his own kingdom unrecognized, and Blink / revelation supports that story even if the execution is somewhat general.

cards.name: Row Past the Sirens
cards.mechanics: Strive; multi-target combat trick; delayed untap
cards.rules:
Strive — This spell costs {1}{W} more to cast for each target beyond the first.
Any number of target creatures each get +1/+1 until end of turn. Untap those creatures at the beginning of the next end step.
cards.story: Book XII / the crew rows past the Sirens with their ears stopped while Odysseus is bound to the mast.
cards.credit: Art: Siren Painter · British Museum · photo Jastrow
cards.storyTarget: Book XII / the crew rows past the Sirens with their ears stopped while Odysseus is bound to the mast.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Book XII / the crew rows past the Sirens with their ears stopped while Odysseus is bound to the mast.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Excellent match: A multi-target vigilance trick literally rallies several rowers at once for a disciplined passage through the danger.

cards.name: Wash the Stranger's Feet
cards.rules: Exile target creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield tapped under its owner's control. You gain 2 life.
cards.story: Book XIX / Eurycleia washes the stranger’s feet, feels Odysseus’s old scar, and recognises the person beneath the disguise.
cards.credit: Art: Greek, Melian, ca. 450 BCE · The Met
cards.storyTarget: Book XIX / foot-washing becomes scar recognition.
cards.flavorStoryElement: The washing itself is ordinary hospitality; recognition happens when touch reveals the old scar.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Blink is an overt Magic abstraction for identity becoming newly legible, while returning tapped and gaining life preserve the bodily care of the scene.

cards.name: Seat the Guest by the Hearth
cards.displayName: Seat the Guest by the Hearth
cards.rules:
Enchant creature an opponent controls
When this Aura enters, create a Food token.
Enchanted creature can't attack or block, and its activated abilities can't be activated.
cards.story: Hospitality ritual / a stranger is seated safely by the household hearth and cared for before being questioned.
cards.credit: Art: “Ulysses in the Palace of Alcinous” · Jean-Jacques Lagrenée · Musée d’art et d’histoire de Narbonne · Wikimedia Commons
cards.changeStatus: candidate2-major-story-v3 · art-review · art-remap-v1 · art-acceptance-v1 · studio-notes-pass-20260921 · mechanics-reconcile-v1-20260924
cards.storyTarget: Seating the guest by the hearth as a concrete act of protection and acceptance.
cards.flavorStoryElement: A guest crosses from exposed stranger to protected member of the household's social space.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Hospitality now changes the board directly: the hostile creature becomes a noncombatant guest, the host supplies Food, and an accumulated pair of Foods converts temporary restraint into permanent white removal.

cards.name: Argos, Who Waited
cards.rules: Vigilance. When Argos enters, scry 1. When Argos dies, return up to one target legendary permanent card with mana value 2 or less from your graveyard to your hand.
cards.story: Book XVII / the neglected old hound Argos recognises Odysseus beneath the beggar disguise after twenty years, then dies.
cards.credit: Art: “Odysseus Recognized by His Dog Argus” · Theodoor van Thulden, after Francesco Primaticcio · Rijksmuseum · Wikimedia Commons
cards.storyTarget: Book XVII / Argos recognises Odysseus beneath the beggar disguise.
cards.flavorStoryElement: The first creature in Ithaca to recognise Odysseus without proof is his dying dog Argos.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Vigilance captures faithful waiting; the death trigger recovers a small legendary permanent, making Argos a literal bridge back to a remembered person or object. Existing Athena art must be replaced.

cards.name: Telemachus Calls the Assembly
cards.rules: Create two 1/1 white Human Citizen creature tokens. If you control a legendary creature, tap up to one target creature an opponent controls and put a stun counter on it.
cards.story: Book II / Telemachus summons Ithaca's first assembly since Odysseus left and publicly challenges the suitors' consumption of his house.
cards.credit: Art: “The Sorrow of Telemachus” · Angelica Kauffmann · The Met
cards.storyTarget: Book II / Telemachus calls Ithaca to assembly and speaks publicly against the suitors.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Telemachus's coming of age first becomes public when he claims the right to speak and asks the community to witness what is happening in his house.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: The assembly now has an efficient board presence at three mana. Citizens physically gather, while a legendary speaker such as Telemachus can publicly check one opposing creature with a stun counter. The art is moved from a generic Pnyx view to a direct Telemachus painting.

cards.name: Steer by the Great Bear
cards.rules: Scry 2. Untap up to one target Vehicle.
cards.story: Book V and broader sailor knowledge / Odysseus is instructed to keep the Great Bear in view while steering across open water.
cards.credit: Art: “A Man Holding an Oar” · Johan Christian Dahl · The Met
cards.storyTarget: Star navigation across the open sea.
cards.storySourceBand: Odyssey Book V / Homeric sailor knowledge
cards.flavorStoryElement: A fixed star pattern becomes practical orientation when no coastline is available.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Scry reads the sky; untapping a Vehicle turns that knowledge into renewed movement. The inland-oar art must be replaced.

cards.name: Loyal Householder
cards.rules: Survival — At the beginning of your second main phase, if Loyal Householder is tapped, untap another target permanent you control.
cards.story: Ithaca / ordinary household labor and endurance during Odysseus’s long absence.
cards.credit: Art: Achilles Painter, ca. 440 BCE · The Met
cards.storyTarget: Ithaca / ordinary household labor and endurance during Odysseus’s long absence.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Ordinary Ithacan household life continuing under strain while Odysseus is absent.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Strong match: Survival rewards a worker who has been active, then restores another permanent, returning this slot from an invented late-prophecy interpreter to grounded Ithacan household connective tissue.

cards.name: Feign Madness
cards.rules: Until end of turn, target creature you control loses all abilities and has base power and toughness 0/4. It gains hexproof until end of turn.
cards.story: Odysseus pretends madness to evade the summons to Troy, making himself appear incapable of command.
cards.credit: Art: “Odysseus Fakes Insanity” · unknown tapestry workshop · Ptuj Ormož Regional Museum
cards.storyTarget: Odysseus pretends madness to evade the summons to Troy, making himself appear incapable of command.
cards.storySourceBand: Epic Cycle / Cypria tradition; Apollodorus Epitome 3.7
cards.flavorStoryElement: Odysseus pretends madness to evade the summons to Troy, making himself appear incapable of command.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: A one-mana Dive Down-style protection spell with a real disguise cost: the creature survives as a harmless 0/4 with hexproof but loses all abilities. The ability loss can also be exploited deliberately.

cards.name: Poseidon's Storm Foretold
cards.rules: Foretell {1}{U}. Tap target creature. It doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step. Draw a card.
cards.story: Book V / Poseidon sees Odysseus at sea after he leaves Calypso and raises the storm that halts his homeward progress.
cards.credit: Art: Theodoor van Thulden · Rijksmuseum
cards.storyTarget: Book V / Poseidon sees Odysseus at sea after he leaves Calypso and raises the storm that halts his homeward progress.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Book V / Poseidon sees Odysseus at sea after he leaves Calypso and raises the storm that halts his homeward progress.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Excellent match: Foretell makes the storm impending; tapping a creature and keeping it from untapping makes the storm physically stop forward motion.

cards.name: Iphigenia's Sacrifice
cards.mechanics: Creature sacrifice; mass tap; card draw
cards.rules:
As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice a nontoken creature.
Tap all creatures your opponents control. Draw two cards.
cards.story: Aulis / Agamemnon chooses the expedition over his daughter; Iphigenia is killed so the Greek fleet can proceed to Troy.
cards.credit: Art: Arnold Houbraken · Rijksmuseum
cards.changeStatus: story-retheme-v2 · art-review · flavor-redesign-v1 · art-sweep-v1 · art-p1-named-v1 · omen-boardwipe-recast-v1 · reference-qa-v1 · template-cleanup-v1 · studio-notes-pass-20260921 · mechanics-reconcile-v1-20260924
cards.storyTarget: Aulis / Iphigenia is actually sacrificed for the war effort so the fleet can sail.
cards.storySourceBand: Aeschylus, Agamemnon / actual sacrifice at Aulis
cards.flavorStoryElement: Agamemnon has Iphigenia killed so the fleet can proceed to war. Her loss buys passage for the expedition; she is not rescued or replaced.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: The mandatory additional-cost sacrifice makes loss precede the campaign’s advance. Mass tapping and two cards are game abstractions for the fleet finally moving; the design does not soften the sacrifice into rescue.

cards.name: Singer at the Hearth
cards.rules: When this creature enters, look at the top four cards of your library. You may reveal an instant, sorcery, or enchantment card from among them and put it into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in any order.
cards.story: Ordinary oral performance / a household or court singer preserves stories through repeated live performance before an audience.
cards.credit: Art: Attributed to the Berlin Painter · The Met
cards.storyTarget: A non-famous singer performing epic material in a lived social setting.
cards.flavorStoryElement: The singer turns the top of the library into a small repertoire of actions and enchantments, mechanically locating stories in performance rather than archives.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: This is ordinary-world bardic glue, deliberately not another Demodocus/Phemius legend.

cards.name: Ordeal of the Sirens
cards.rules:
Enchant creature
When Ordeal of the Sirens enters, tap enchanted creature.
Survival — At the beginning of your second main phase, if enchanted creature is tapped, put a +1/+1 counter on it. Then if it has three or more +1/+1 counters on it, sacrifice this Aura.
When you sacrifice this Aura, manifest fate.
cards.story: Book XII / Odysseus survives the Sirens only by planning the trial in advance, hearing the song while bound to the mast as his crew rows on.
cards.credit: Art: “Ulysses and the Sirens” · John William Waterhouse · National Gallery of Victoria · Wikimedia Commons
cards.changeStatus: replacement-slot · survivor-ordeals-v3-tuned · restored-to-14A2-20260922 · mechanics-reconcile-v1-20260924 · studio-notes-20260925-v1 · wave-a-live-20260926
cards.storyTarget: Book XII / Odysseus survives the Sirens only by planning the trial in advance, hearing the song while bound to the mast as his crew rows on.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Book XII / Odysseus survives the Sirens only by planning the trial in advance, hearing the song while bound to the mast as his crew rows on.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Excellent match: the Aura grants Survival directly, the creature grows through repeated successful second-main tapped checks, and the completion payoff feeds a major Odyssey draft lane without overwhelming the three-turn setup.

cards.name: Read the Hidden Course
cards.mechanics: Quest counters; exile; face-down; card draw
cards.rules: Whenever you cast a spell from exile or turn a face-down permanent face up, put a quest counter on this enchantment. This ability triggers only once each turn. Then if it has three or more quest counters on it, sacrifice it. When you do, draw two cards.
cards.story: Practical navigation and interpretation: repeatedly finding a usable route through signs, concealed information and roads not taken.
cards.credit: Art: “Sonata No. 6 (Sonata of the Stars): Andante” · Mikalojus Konstantinas Čiurlionis · M. K. Čiurlionis National Museum of Art · Wikimedia Commons
cards.storyTarget: Reading stars, signs and concealed possibilities across the voyage.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Repeated exile or face-down play becomes a navigational challenge whose completion produces a burst of knowledge.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: This makes Manifest Fate/exile feel like a journey rather than a bookkeeping engine. Leucothea art is only a placeholder for a broader navigation identity.

cards.name: Voyage's End
cards.rules: Return target creature to its owner's hand. Scry 1.
cards.story: Book XIII / the Phaeacians set the sleeping Odysseus on Ithaca with his gifts; he wakes unable at first to recognize home.
cards.credit: Art: Theodoor van Thulden, after Francesco Primaticcio · Rijksmuseum
cards.changeStatus: flavor-redesign-v1 · art-review · art-sweep-v1 · art-p1-upgrade-v1 · task9-scheria-pruning-v1 · homeward-package-reclassification-v1 · studio-notes-20260922-v1
cards.storyTarget: Book XIII / the Phaeacians set the sleeping Odysseus on Ithaca with his gifts; he wakes unable at first to recognize home.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Book XIII / the Phaeacians set the sleeping Odysseus on Ithaca with his gifts; he wakes unable at first to recognize home.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Strong match after redesign: the card identity is specific to Book XIII / the Phaeacians set the sleeping Odysseus on Ithaca with his gifts; he wakes unable at first to recognize home., and its mechanics now reinforce the story beat rather than serving as a generic Greek analogue.

cards.name: Hubris
cards.rules: Return target creature and all Auras attached to it to their owners' hands.
cards.story: Book IX / after escaping Polyphemus, Odysseus boasts his true name and gives the Cyclops the knowledge needed to call Poseidon's vengeance.
cards.credit: Art: Theodoor van Thulden · Rijksmuseum
cards.storyTarget: Book IX / after escaping Polyphemus, Odysseus boasts his true name and gives the Cyclops the knowledge needed to call Poseidon's vengeance.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Book IX / after escaping Polyphemus, Odysseus boasts his true name and gives the Cyclops the knowledge needed to call Poseidon's vengeance.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Excellent match after redesign: the card identity and mechanics directly dramatize Book IX / after escaping Polyphemus, Odysseus boasts his true name and gives the Cyclops the knowledge needed to call Poseidon's vengeance.

cards.name: Cutting Raft Timbers
cards.rules: Search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle. You may return target Vehicle card from your graveyard to your hand.
cards.story: Book V / Odysseus cuts and prepares timber before shaping the raft that will carry him away from Ogygia.
cards.credit: Art: Willem Basse · Rijksmuseum
cards.changeStatus: candidate2-major-story-v2 · art-review · art-remap-v1 · art-acceptance-v1 · studio-notes-20260922-v1 · studio-notes-20260925-v1
cards.storyTarget: Book V / felling and preparing timber for the raft.
cards.flavorStoryElement: The voyage only resumes after sustained practical carpentry, not another divine shortcut.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: The land ramp represents timber/resources; optional Vehicle recovery lets a wrecked craft become a new attempt. Kept outside the capped Ogygia identity accounting as primary Build-Raft ownership.

cards.name: Paris, Prince of Troy
cards.rules:
Reach
Whenever Paris attacks, it deals 1 damage to target creature defending player controls. That creature can't block this turn.
cards.story: Trojan War / Paris as the archer prince whose choices help cause the war and whose battlefield role is ranged and indirect.
cards.storyTarget: Paris as the archer prince of Troy, fighting indirectly rather than as another front-line champion.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Paris's ranged, indirect battlefield role contrasts sharply with Hector's direct defense of Troy.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Reach and the attack ping make Paris feel like an archer who shapes combat without becoming another large martial legend.

cards.name: Bolt the Doors
cards.rules: Tap up to two target creatures. Creatures you control get +1/+1 until end of turn.
cards.story: Books XXI–XXII / the palace is physically closed down around the suitors before escape or reinforcement can undo Odysseus's plan.
cards.credit: Art: “Odysseus Battling the Suitors” · Lovis Corinth · Berlinische Galerie · Wikimedia Commons
cards.changeStatus: candidate2-major-story-v2 · art-review · art-remap-v1 · art-acceptance-v1 · studio-notes-20260922-v1 · mechanics-reconcile-v1-20260924
cards.storyTarget: Books XXI–XXII / closing the palace exits before the reckoning.
cards.flavorStoryElement: The locked hall turns a household interior into a controlled battlefield.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: A simple common tempo action deepens the locked-hall sequence without adding another named suitor or a third bow-contest card.

cards.name: Trace the Omen
cards.rules: Look at the top three cards of your library. Put one into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in any order. If you don't own a card in exile, exile a card from your hand.
cards.story: Omens are not only seen; they must be followed through implications, competing readings and the consequences of earlier choices.
cards.credit: Art: “Tiresias Appears to Ulysses during the Sacrifice” · Henry Fuseli · Albertina · Wikimedia Commons
cards.storyTarget: Omens are not only seen; they must be followed through implications, competing readings and the consequences of earlier choices.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Omens are not only seen; they must be followed through implications, competing readings and the consequences of earlier choices.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Uncommon rebuild: structural role preserved while obscure/sequel identity remains cut.

cards.name: Suitor's Extortion
cards.rules: Target opponent discards a card. If you control a tapped creature, that player loses 2 life.
cards.story: Suitors
cards.credit: Art: “Terracotta amphora (jar): revelers” · Attributed to the Acheloös Painter · The Met
cards.storyTarget: Suitors
cards.flavorStoryElement: Books I–II / the suitors consume Odysseus’s household and pressure his family
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Strong match: the card clearly represents Books I–II / the suitors consume Odysseus’s household and pressure his family, and Discard supports that story even if the execution is somewhat general.

cards.name: Elpenor's Funeral Due
cards.rules: Target creature gets -2/-2 until end of turn. If a card left your graveyard this turn, it gets -4/-4 instead.
cards.story: Books XI–XII / after Elpenor’s shade demands burial, Odysseus returns to Aeaea and performs the funeral rites he owes him.
cards.credit: Art: Theodoor van Thulden · Rijksmuseum
cards.storyTarget: Books XI–XII / after Elpenor’s shade demands burial, Odysseus returns to Aeaea and performs the funeral rites he owes him.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Books XI–XII / after Elpenor’s shade demands burial, Odysseus returns to Aeaea and performs the funeral rites he owes him.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Excellent match: The removal becomes stronger only after the graveyard has been disturbed, tying the spell to the obligation created by speaking with the unburied dead.

cards.name: Call the Shades Forward
cards.rules: Mill two cards. You may return a creature card from your graveyard to your hand. If you do, target opponent sacrifices a tapped creature.
cards.story: Book XI / Odysseus pours libations and sacrificial blood into the trench, then calls individual shades forward to speak.
cards.credit: Art: Theodoor van Thulden · Rijksmuseum
cards.storyTarget: Book XI / the poured offerings and blood-trench call the shades forward one by one.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Libations and blood open the boundary; individual shades are then allowed forward to speak.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Excellent match: The spell moves cards toward the graveyard, brings one dead figure forward, and makes the encounter exact a blood price without consuming one of the set’s fifteen Saga slots.

cards.name: Penelope Questions the Beggar
cards.rules: Draw two cards, then discard a card. If you discarded a legendary card this way, scry 2.
cards.story: Book XIX / Penelope questions the disguised Odysseus at length about her absent husband, testing the stranger's story without knowing who sits before her.
cards.credit: Art: Walter Paget · La Odisea (1910) · Wikimedia Commons
cards.storyTarget: Book XIX / Penelope interrogates the disguised Odysseus about himself.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Penelope's questioning is intelligent information-gathering, not passive waiting.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Draw-discard models extracting a story and testing it; discarding a legend sharpens the scry because a famous identity is exactly what is being examined.

cards.name: Betray the Hidden Armory
cards.rules:
Gift a Treasure
Destroy target artifact or creature an opponent controls. If the gift wasn't promised, you lose 2 life.
cards.story: Book XXII / Melanthius opens the hidden stores to the suitors, turning the household’s own resources against its defenders.
cards.credit: Photo: George E. Koronaios · National Archaeological Museum, Athens · Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
cards.changeStatus: candidate2-major-story-v3 · art-review · art-remap-v1 · art-acceptance-v1 · studio-notes-20260922-v1 · source-repair-v1-20260924
cards.storyTarget: Book XXII / Melanthius uses access to the hidden armory to equip the suitors.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Melanthius converts the household’s stored arms into resources for the trapped suitors.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: The scene now creates a real decision: give the opposing side a material resource, as Melanthius does, or take the life penalty yourself. The flexible removal role remains intact, while Gift makes the betrayal direction explicit.

cards.name: Asphyxiate
cards.rules: Destroy target untapped creature.
cards.story: Book XXII / Odysseus begins the slaughter by shooting Antinous while the suitor is still drinking at the feast.
cards.credit: Art: “Ulysses Killing Antinous” · Tako Hajo Jelgersma · British Museum · Wikimedia Commons
cards.storyTarget: Book XXII / Odysseus begins the slaughter by shooting Antinous while the suitor is still drinking at the feast.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Book XXII / Odysseus begins the slaughter by shooting Antinous while the suitor is still drinking at the feast.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Excellent match after redesign: the card identity and mechanics directly dramatize Book XXII / Odysseus begins the slaughter by shooting Antinous while the suitor is still drinking at the feast.

cards.name: Eumaeus Shares His Supper
cards.mechanics: Gift a Food; Food; arrival counter
cards.rules:
Gift a Food
Create a Food token. Put a +1/+1 counter on up to one target creature that entered under your control this turn. If the gift was promised, you gain 3 life.
cards.story: Book XIV / Eumaeus feeds and shelters the disguised Odysseus despite his own poverty.
cards.credit: Art: James Parker, after John Flaxman · Rijksmuseum
cards.changeStatus: candidate2-major-story-v2 · art-review · art-remap-v1 · art-acceptance-v1 · mechanics-reconcile-v1-20260924 · wave-a-live-20260926
cards.storyTarget: Book XIV / Eumaeus feeds and shelters the disguised Odysseus.
cards.flavorStoryElement: The poorest major host in the poem still fulfils guest-friendship better than the wealthy suitors.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Food makes the meal literal; the permanent counter rewards a newly arrived guest instead of wasting a temporary attack bonus on a creature with summoning sickness.

cards.name: Loyal Cowherd
cards.rules: Survival — At the beginning of your second main phase, if this creature is tapped, put a +1/+1 counter on up to one other target creature with power 2 or less.
cards.story: Ithaca / ordinary herd-workers whose continued service keeps the absent household functioning and contrasts with the servants who side with the suitors.
cards.credit: Art: “Cattle Herd in the Campagna with a Mounted Herdsman” · Anton Romako · Private collection; reproduced by Dorotheum · Wikimedia Commons
cards.storyTarget: Ordinary loyal livestock work within the Ithacan estate.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Loyalty is shown as continuing the work rather than making a speech about loyalty.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: The Survival trigger rewards a worker who actually taps to act and then strengthens another modest creature.

cards.name: Row Through the Gale
cards.rules: Whenever one or more Vehicles you control attack, put a quest counter on this enchantment. This ability triggers only once each turn. Then if it has three or more quest counters on it, sacrifice it. When you do, create two Treasure tokens, then exile the top two cards of your library. You may play one of them until the end of your next turn.
cards.story: A crew proves itself by repeatedly driving ships through difficult weather rather than by one named storm episode.
cards.credit: Art: “Juno Ordering Aeolus to Unleash the Winds” · Louis Jean Jacques Durameau · The Met
cards.storyTarget: Repeated ship handling through bad weather and difficult passages.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Three successful Vehicle attacks represent sustained seamanship; the payoff converts that accumulated momentum into supplies and temporary access to new options.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: This avoids consuming an Aeolus or Book V storm slot. Existing wind art can be reconsidered as atmospheric rather than episode-specific.

cards.name: Laestrygonian Glutton
cards.rules: When this creature enters, an opponent may put two +1/+1 counters on it. If they don't, it deals 3 damage to any target.
cards.story: Laestrygonians
cards.credit: Art: “The King of the Lestrigens Seizing One of the Companions of Ulysses” · James Parker, after John Flaxman · Rijksmuseum
cards.storyTarget: Laestrygonians
cards.flavorStoryElement: Laestrygonians
cards.flavorMatchRationale: Strong match: the card clearly represents Laestrygonians, and Opponent choice / direct damage supports that story even if the execution is somewhat general.

cards.name: Invoke the Muse

cards.name: The Song Outlives the Singer
cards.rules:
Whenever you cast a Saga or legendary spell, scry 1. This ability triggers only once each turn.
At the beginning of your end step, if a Saga or legendary permanent you controlled left the battlefield this turn, draw a card.
cards.archetypes: WU / UR / GU — legends / enchantments / stories
cards.story: The oral epic / singers and heroes pass away, but performance, repetition, and audience memory carry their stories into the next telling.
cards.credit: Art: “Blind Homer” · J.-B.-R.-U. Massard, after François Gérard · National Gallery of Art
cards.storyTarget: Oral epic as a living system in which the story survives its individual performer and subjects.
cards.storySourceBand: Homeric oral-performance tradition / later visual analogue
cards.flavorStoryElement: A singer is mortal, while the repeated song becomes communal memory and survives the departure of both performer and hero.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: This final rare raises legend density with a singular cultural institution rather than another character version. It rewards both Sagas and legends and naturally turns their departure into remembered cards.

cards.name: Well-Tended Vineyard
cards.rules:
{T}: Add {C}.
{2}, {T}: Create a Food token. Activate only as a sorcery.
cards.archetypes: All / GW / BG — Food / artifacts / attrition
cards.story: Book XXIV / Laertes’s vineyard and carefully cultivated farm turn long-term labor into ordinary household provision.
cards.credit: Art: “Olive Grove” · John Singer Sargent · Indianapolis Museum of Art · Wikimedia Commons
cards.storyTarget: Book XXIV / Laertes’s vineyard as productive household land.
cards.flavorStoryElement: The source gives a cultivated vineyard and farm whose value comes from patient tending and provision, not a specifically terraced olive harvest.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: The Food-producing land role is retained, while the new identity removes unsupported terrace and olive-harvest claims and anchors the card to Laertes’s explicitly cultivated estate.

cards.name: Athena and Odysseus, Minds Alike
cards.story: Across the Odyssey, Athena and Odysseus repeatedly recognise in one another the same preference for disguise, planning, testing and adaptive intelligence.
cards.credit: Art: “Athena Appearing to Odysseus to Reveal the Island of Ithaca” · Giuseppe Bottani · Collection not stated · Wikimedia Commons
cards.storyTarget: Athena + Odysseus as the poem's central alliance of cunning.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Athena + Odysseus as the poem's central alliance of cunning.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: The ETB creates two possible roads, ward protects the plan, and the recurring loot rewards turning hidden/exiled possibility into action.

cards.name: Zeus, Keeper of Oaths
cards.rules:
Indestructible
As long as your devotion to red and white is less than seven, Zeus isn't a creature.
Whenever one or more creatures attack you, Zeus deals 2 damage to their controller and you gain 2 life. This ability triggers only once each turn.
cards.story: Zeus as guarantor of oaths and guest-right: violence and broken social obligation ultimately sit beneath a divine order larger than any one household.
cards.credit: Art: Felice Giani · Smithsonian
cards.storyTarget: Zeus in his oath/xenia role rather than Trojan battlefield role.
cards.flavorStoryElement: Zeus in his oath/xenia role rather than Trojan battlefield role.
cards.flavorMatchRationale: A broad mythic god rewards defensive social order and punishes open aggression without reopening the Trojan god package.

coverage.name: Seat the Guest by the Hearth
coverage.notes: Public-domain rights workaround found: DISC-021 records Roscher’s reproduction of the 19th-century Overbeck drawing of the exact named Telegonus/Circe fragment. flavorAudit.rubric: 0–5: 5 scene/character/object is taught through identity and mechanics; 4 strong direct match; 3 recognizable but generic; 2 weak/analogue; 1 mostly cosmetic; 0 no defensible specific element.

policy.protagonistException: 3–4 versions only when each version represents a materially distinct dramatic state and mechanical identity.
policy.antiPattern: Do not spend multiple named legendary slots on the same scene/state merely at different rarities.

Odysseus.rationale: Four materially different states: wandering/voyage engine, Nobody/Cyclops deception, Thesprotian war-king, and late return to Ithaca.

Penelope.rationale: Patient household ruler, mythic weaving centerpiece, and post-suitor household anchor. Redundant waiting-state version was removed.

Telegonus.rationale: Two uncommon signposts encode voyage/search and stranger/heir states across different archetypes; rare stingray-spear version is the fatal climax.

Telemachus.rationale: Young heir, returned fighting son/RW signpost, and post-Odyssey heir are distinct chronological and mechanical states.

Antinous.rationale: WB uncommon establishes suitor signpost identity; mono-black rare is the consuming-household antagonist.

Apollo.rationale: Post-Odyssey separator of divine combat and Trojan defender are separate narrative functions.

Ares.rationale: Post-Odyssey rout of the Thesprotians and Trojan-war god embodiment are separate uses.

Athena.rationale: Core Odyssey guide and later opponent of Ares are different narrative eras and jobs.

Calypso.rationale: GU uncommon signpost plus mythic Ogygia/exile centerpiece.

Circe.rationale: UB uncommon signpost plus mythic prepared transformation centerpiece.

Tiresias.rationale: UB uncommon is archetype signpost; rare foretell version is the premium prophecy card.

survivorOrdealCycle.template: Enchant creature; the Aura grants the enchanted creature Survival. A successful Survival trigger adds a +1/+1 counter; once the creature has three or more +1/+1 counters, the Ordeal's controller sacrifices the Aura. Sacrifice payoffs are tuned to roughly one card plus one thematic unit of value.
survivorOrdealCycle.designIntent: Five uncommon {1}{C} Auras riffing on the Theros Ordeals. They turn tapping/attacking/crewing into a three-stage trial and bridge Survival into Odyssey's household, Manifest Fate, graveyard, exile-casting, Food and ramp themes.
